practices.practice: Read the Azure DocumentDB connection string from an environment-backed config (.env or similar) at startup and fail fast with a clear error if it's missing.
practices.prior_belief: Read the Azure DocumentDB (MongoDB API) connection string from an environment-backed config (.env or config file) at startup and fail fast with a clear error message if it's missing or malformed; never hard-code or commit the secret into source control.

practices.practice: Create and reuse a single MongoClient instance (process-wide singleton) and tune connection-pool parameters (e.g., maxPoolSize) for your deployment scenario rather than creating a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Reuse a single MongoClient across the whole Node.js process (singleton) and rely on connection pooling instead of creating a new client per request; configure maxPoolSize (e.g. 50–200) to match expected concurrency.

practices.practice: Always require TLS on connections to Azure DocumentDB and do not disable certificate validation in production; ensure the connection string includes TLS (tls=true) and your runtime has a valid CA bundle.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce TLS in the connection string (e.g., tls=true or ssl=true) and verify server certificates to protect the connection string and data in transit.

practices.practice: Tune connection-pool parameters according to hosting: small maxPoolSize and short maxIdleTimeMS for serverless, larger pools (50+) and longer idle times for long-running OLTP servers; set timeouts (connectTimeoutMS, socketTimeoutMS) appropriate to expected latencies.

Enable SDK retry semantics (retryReads/retryWrites) and implement application-level retries with exponential backoff and jitter for transient errors and 429 responses, honouring Retry-After when present.
practices.prior_belief: Respect rate limiting and throttling: handle 429 responses by reading Retry-After headers (or SDK-provided retry metadata), back off and retry with exponential jitter, and surface meaningful errors to the caller if retries fail.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB throttling Retry-After 429 best practices

practices.practice: Create a vector index on your embedding field using the cosmosSearch operator, specifying the index kind (vector-diskann/vector-hnsw/vector-ivf), the embedding dimensions, and the similarity metric; the index's dimensions and similarity must match the embeddings you insert.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index DiskANN create index cosmosSearch dimensions similarity

practices.practice: Prefer DiskANN for production-scale vector workloads on M30+ clusters and tune DiskANN build/query parameters (maxDegree, lBuild at index-build time; lSearch at query time) to trade recall vs latency.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB DiskANN lBuild lSearch maxDegree guidance

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings to unit length when using COS (cosine) similarity and record the embedding model name and dimension as metadata alongside each vector so you can detect model drift and safely re-embed.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize embeddings to unit length when using cosine similarity (i.e., divide vector by its L2 norm before storing or before query) to make cosine or dot-product comparisons consistent.

practices.practice: When querying vectors use the $search aggregation stage with the cosmosSearch operator (knn-style), keep lSearch >= k, tune lSearch for recall/latency, and use the cosmosSearch filter option to push predicates into the ANN search rather than post-filtering.
practices.prior_belief: When the vector index supports parameters, tune search-time parameter efSearch (or scan_k/ef) to meet the recall/latency target (e.g., raise efSearch for better recall); persist the chosen value in config and document the recall/latency observed.

practices.practice: Vectors must be stored as a numeric array (number[]) for DocumentDB vector indexes to index them; using a mismatched type prevents indexing and makes documents non-indexed for vector search.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index vector must be number[] type

practices.practice: Use product quantization or half-precision indexing (fp16) to reduce vector index memory and support higher dimensional vectors when supported by the index type.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB product quantization half-precision vector index guidance

practices.practice: Use server-side aggregation pipelines ($match, $unwind, $group, $sort, $limit) to compute co-purchase counts and other aggregations rather than pulling large datasets to the client.
practices.prior_belief: Use server-side aggregation pipelines (e.g., $match, $unwind, $group, $sort, $limit) to compute co-purchase counts and session aggregation rather than pulling large amounts of data to the app.

practices.practice: Use a TTL index (expireAfterSeconds) on a Date field to automatically expire ephemeral session documents; the indexed field must be a Date and TTL indexes cannot be compound or multikey.
practices.prior_belief: Persist per-session memory in a dedicated sessions collection with a TTL index (expireAfterSeconds) for ephemeral memory and index sessionId as unique; keep session documents small (ids and short vectors or references).

practices.practice: Project only the fields you need in queries (limit returned fields) to reduce RU consumption and network bandwidth, especially for large documents or when returning many results.
practices.prior_belief: Limit the projection returned by queries (project only the fields you need, e.g., productId, title, price, embeddingExists flag) to reduce RU consumption and network bandwidth.

practices.practice: Instrument RU consumption and latency in development and use explain('executionStats') to validate index usage and RU efficiency before large-scale ingestion or production queries.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument RU and latency metrics in the app (log RU charges returned in response metadata) and validate index plans (explain) in development so that queries are RU-efficient before running large-scale ingestion or search.
practices.how_found: documentdb-query-optimizer; Azure Cosmos DB bulk and RU docs

practices.practice: Use unique indexes to enforce uniqueness for primary keys used by the app (e.g., productId, sessionId) and use upserts carefully for idempotent seeding.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce uniqueness with unique indexes for primary keys used by the app (productId, sessionId) to prevent duplicates during concurrent seed runs; use upserts carefully when idempotent seeding is required.

practices.practice: When building or rebuilding large vector indexes, document expected storage/compute cost and avoid frequent full rebuilds; prefer techniques such as product quantization, half-precision, or incremental updates where supported.
practices.prior_belief: When creating vector indexes, document the index’s storage/compute cost and perform an index-building dry-run on a small subset; avoid rebuilding very large indexes frequently—prefer incremental updates where supported.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index build cost guidance

practices.practice: Protect external API keys (e.g., OpenAI) and other secrets the same way as DB credentials; do not embed sensitive or PII data in requests to third-party embedding/LLM services without policy review.
practices.prior_belief: Protect API keys used for external LLM/embedding services (OPENAI_API_KEY) the same way as DB secrets, and avoid embedding raw user or personally identifiable data in embeddings sent to third-party services unless policy-reviewed.

practices.practice: For large-scale ingestion prefer bulk-executor/SDK bulk APIs or distributed import tools (Spark connector) and implement throughput-control, auto-tuned micro-batching, concurrency limits and retries to avoid sustained 429 throttling.

practices.practice: Use the DocumentDB/MongoDB explain API (.explain('executionStats')) or MCP explain_operation to validate index usage and confirm you avoid COLLSCAN before running production workloads.
Prefer pushing filters into the cosmosSearch query (the filter option) so the ANN engine prunes candidates early rather than post-filtering which may discard most top-k results.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB

practices.practice: Only one vector per indexed path is supported and you can create only one vector index per vector path; plan schema accordingly to avoid conflict.
practices.source_name: Integrated vector store in Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB vector index one vector per path one index per path

practices.practice: Store embedding metadata (model name, dims, embeddingVersion) with documents to detect mismatches and trigger re-embedding or index rebuilds when models change.
When ingesting embeddings at scale, validate vector dimensions match the index and reject or normalize inconsistent vectors before inserting to avoid silent search corruption.

practices.practice: Use server-side throughput and RU metrics and the SDK response diagnostics to monitor RU charges per operation and detect high-cost queries during development.

practices.practice: When using local DocumentDB Gateway for development, keep TLS relaxed only for local dev and drive TLS relaxation from environment variables rather than hard-coding tlsAllowInvalidCertificates in application code.
For production HA and DR, use in-region availability zones for high availability and add cross-region replicas for business-continuity; understand the backup and SLA implications per tier.

Prefer server-side libraries and bulk APIs (or distributed tools like Spark connector) for very large imports rather than naive insert loops from a single client machine, and if you must use single-machine ingestion, implement throughput control and concurrency limits.

practices.practice: Use explain() and index statistics (listIndexes / $indexStats) to maintain a small, relevant set of indexes (typically 5–15) and to detect unused or redundant indexes that add write cost.
Use the MCP or driver explain tools to verify vector-search plans and to project the searchScore (meta: 'searchScore') when you intend to re-rank results based on ANN scores.

practices.practice: Store embedding vectors with consistent numeric types and shapes and validate them before insertion (no mixed-length or mixed-type vectors), though Azure docs require number[] but do not mandate a single float width (e.g., float32) explicitly.
practices.prior_belief: Store embeddings as a consistent numeric array type (prefer float32 sized values) and avoid mixed numeric types; validate types at ingest to keep index behavior predictable.

practices.practice: The public Azure DocumentDB documentation does not prescribe a two-stage recommendation pipeline (ANN candidate set then server-side re-rank using co-purchase frequency); build such a pipeline yourself and rely on server-side aggregation for signals if desired.
practices.prior_belief: Use a two-stage recommendation pipeline: (1) ANN vector search to produce a candidate set (e.g., top 100), (2) re-rank candidates using co-purchase frequency and session memory (server-side aggregation where possible) before returning top 5.

practices.practice: Using deterministic synthetic embeddings in tests and development when external embedding APIs are unavailable is a practical developer pattern but is not documented as an official Azure DocumentDB best practice.
practices.prior_belief: For development and CI when OpenAI keys are not present, use deterministic synthetic embeddings (fixed RNG seed) to make tests reproducible and validate end-to-end behavior without external API calls; guard real API usage behind an env flag.

practices.practice: There is no Azure DocumentDB public guidance that specifies a graceful application-level fallback strategy if a vector index is missing; implement an application fallback (popularity/co-purchase) yourself and log missing-index conditions.
practices.prior_belief: Provide a graceful fallback if the vector index or vector query fails (e.g., index not present): return top co-purchased/popularity-based recommendations and log the missing-index condition for remediation.

practices.practice: Public Azure DocumentDB guidance does not emphasize avoiding long-lived multi-document transactions for high-throughput recommendation flows; treat cross-document transactions as rare and keep them short when required.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid long-lived transactions for recommendation flows—use idempotent single-document writes or small multi-document operations; if cross-document consistency is required, keep transactions short and rare.
